audits.title: Prevention of needle-stick injury among nurses in an acute ward of a hospital: a best practice implementation project.
audits.standard: Five JBI audit criteria for best practice in prevention of needle-stick injuries (JBI PACES and GRiP)
audits.setting: Five acute wards of a hospital in central Taiwan (Taichung Veterans General Hospital)

cycle1.result: Compliance 14-15% for use of safety-engineered devices and safe use and disposal of needles; safety needle use 16%, procedure awareness 14%, no recapping 47%, disposal in sharps box 75%.

audits.intervention: Multiple strategies over 20 weeks, including standardised education and training on safe use and disposal of sharps.

cycle2.result: Compliance ranged from 40 to 96.6%; safety needle use 95.5%, procedure awareness 96%, no recapping 85%, disposal in sharps box 80%.

audits.other_findings: Baseline needle-stick injury incidence was 5.6% in the acute ward.
audits.citation: Huang HM, Chien HC, Lin WL, Chang CH, Chang MY, Su JY, et al.. Prevention of needle-stick injury among nurses in an acute ward of a hospital: a best practice implementation project. JBI Evid Implement. 2022;20(2):134-143. doi:10.1097/xeb.0000000000000294. PMID: 34581305.

audits.title: Improving Knowledge of Needle-Stick Injury Prevention: A Two-Cycle Clinical Audit From Sudan.
audits.standard: Globally recognised occupational health standards for NSI prevention and post-exposure prophylaxis

cycle1.result: HBV known as commonest pathogen: doctors 15.8%, nurses 15.8%, technicians 65%; PEP understood as medication: doctors 52.6%, nurses 52.6%, technicians 25%; awareness of reporting system: doctors 89.5%, technicians 50%.

audits.intervention: Structured teaching sessions, posters, departmental reinforcement and guideline summaries.

cycle2.result: HBV: doctors 81.2%, nurses 100%, technicians 100%; PEP: doctors 93.8%, nurses 100%, technicians 100%; wound washing awareness 100% in nurses and technicians; reporting system awareness: doctors 12.5%, technicians 5%.

audits.other_findings: Awareness of formal reporting fell sharply and refresher training participation declined across groups. Knowledge assessed by questionnaire.
audits.citation: Mohammed Hamed FJ, Kheder M, Haroon OS, Abdelrahman AOM, Yousif M, Yagoub IYA, et al.. Improving Knowledge of Needle-Stick Injury Prevention: A Two-Cycle Clinical Audit From Sudan. Cureus. 2025;17(11):e96964. doi:10.7759/cureus.96964. PMID: 41278075.

audits.title: Awareness and Perspectives of Doctors on Needle Stick Injuries at Port Sudan Teaching Hospital: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.standard: Standards on safety device use, no recapping, sharps container practice, immediate first aid, reporting and PEP

cycle1.result: HBV recognised as bloodborne risk 33/53 (62.3%); correct PEP initiation within 72 hours 18/53 (34.0%).

audits.intervention: Education sessions, practical workshops, quick-reference materials, better access to safety-engineered devices and a non-punitive reporting culture
audits.other_findings: Relied largely on self-report; HCV and HIV risk communication still needed work.
audits.citation: Abdelbagi AY, Widaa Mohamed AA, Yousif ASA, Ahmed Osman Mohamed A, Abdalla M, Saeed Abdelrahim Saeed S, et al.. Awareness and Perspectives of Doctors on Needle Stick Injuries at Port Sudan Teaching Hospital: A Quality Improvement Project. Cureus. 2025;17(10):e95617. doi:10.7759/cureus.95617. PMID: 41322947.

audits.title: Audit of needlestick injuries in dental and dermatology sections: insights and strategies for safer practices.
audits.standard: Safety protocols for sharps handling (OSHA hierarchy of controls)
audits.setting: Dental and dermatology sections, Aga Khan University Hospital, Karachi

cycle1.result: 15 needlestick and sharps injuries, 12 (80%) among dental staff.

audits.intervention: Workshops and training sessions based on root cause analysis and the OSHA hierarchy of controls.
audits.other_findings: Main causes were improper needle handling and recapping in dentistry and scalpel blade cuts in dermatology.
audits.citation: Sadiq A, Khalid T, Umer F, Yaqoob H, Siddiqui HK. Audit of needlestick injuries in dental and dermatology sections: insights and strategies for safer practices. J Pak Med Assoc. 2026;76(Suppl 1)(3):S65-S70. doi:10.47391/jpma.aku-10surg-13. PMID: 42363380.
